rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says the angels were ordered to prostrate before Adam's creation was completed, immediately after the spirit was breathed into him.
rows.anchor: أن الأمر بالسجود له كان قبل إتمام خلقه وأن السجود كان عقب النفخ , وبه صرح البغوي في تفسيره

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: To reconcile 7:11, he says creation and fashioning concern Adam alone, expressed plurally because he is mankind's father; alternatively, ثم can mean و without sequence.
rows.anchor: وبه صرح البغوي في تفسيره , وأجاب عن قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: Yaman defines fashioning as opening the ears, eyes, and fingers.
rows.anchor: والتصوير شق السمع والبصر والأصابع - قاله يمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making Adam even means adjusting and completing his form and preparing it to receive the spirit.
rows.anchor: والتسوية تعديل الخلق وإتمامه وتهيئته لنفخ الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural creation and fashioning may mean a near and deliberate ordering for emergence from nonexistence; the Torah's two creation statements can thus mean existence and prior preparation for intended ends.
rows.anchor: فهذا خلق بمعنى الإيجاد , وذلك بمعنى التقدير القريب منه - والتهيئة لقبول الغايات

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi places the command to prostrate after the angels are informed of the names.
rows.anchor: ومشى البيضاوي على أن الأمر بالسجود كان بعد الإنباء بالأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers placing prostration after the announcement: before it, the angels' prostration would be faith in the unseen; afterward, Adam's learned superiority was evident with certainty.
rows.anchor: على أن المشي عليه أولى من جهة المعنى , لأن سجود الملائكة عليهم السلام قبل يكون إيمانا بالغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative order first establishes Adam's knowledge as the proof of his merit, then records the angels' submission and the favor of prostration for his descendants, preserving a clear sequence of argument and favors.
rows.anchor: فذكر ما آتاه من العلم , فلما فرغ من محاجتهم بما أوجب إذعانهم ذكر بنيه بنعمة السجود له

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: After displaying Adam's knowledge, vicegerency, and prostration, God shows Adam's capacity to err and return in repentance, contrasting his return with Iblis's refusal and the angels' submission.
rows.anchor: ليظهر فضل آدم في حال مخالفته على إبليس في حال إبائه مما يبدو على آدم من الرجوع بالتوبة كحال رجوع الملائكة بالتسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God begins by recalling favors that Israel met with ingratitude and His forbearance and pardon, then commands covenant-keeping, especially following Muhammad and believing his Book.
rows.anchor: ابتدأ سبحانه بتذكيرهم بما خصهم به عن النوع الآدمي من النعم التي كانوا يقابلونها بالكفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel is the one whom God honored, and whose children He honored for his sake.
rows.anchor: أي الذي شرفته وشرفت بنيه من أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering may be by tongue or heart; the author transmits al-Kisa'i's distinction that kasra is tongue and damma is heart, whose opposites are silence and forgetfulness respectively.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي : هو بالكسر باللسان وبالضم بالقلب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines remembrance as bringing to mind something previously forgotten.
rows.anchor: من الذكر وهو استحضار ما سبقه النسيان

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: A blessing gives a person what suits body and soul, including what suits the inner and outer self and its household relations.
rows.anchor: وهي إنالة الشخص ما يوافق نفسه وبدنه وعند المتفطن ما يوافق باطنه وظاهره

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali draws a subtle distinction in the form of allati: its initial element signals an inward, descending, imagined, ambiguous meaning clarified by its relative clause.
rows.anchor: تي منها إشارة لباطن نازل متخيل مبهم تفسره صلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The special blessing was guidance through scriptures and messengers, saving Israel from humiliation in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وتلك النعمة الشريفة هي الإتيان بالهدى من الكتب والرسل الذي استنقذتكم به

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali explains fulfilling a covenant as an act that follows prior knowledge.
rows.anchor: من الوفاء وهو عمل لاحق بمقتضى تقدم علم سابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel's covenant is adherence to revelation and following Muhammad and those whom they were instructed to follow after him.
rows.anchor: الذي أخذته عليكم في لزوم ما أنزل إليكم من متابعة نبيكم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines covenant as a prior, private undertaking in a matter assigned to someone.
rows.anchor: والعهد التقدم في الشيء خفية اختصاصا لمن يتقدم له فيه

rows.speaker: الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Al-Isfahani defines covenant as preserving and tending something continually.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصفهاني : حفظ الشيء ومراعاته حالا فحالا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says the root sense of covenant is protecting something and renewing the pledge to it.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل : أصله الاحتفاظ بالشيء وإجداد العهد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's fulfillment of their covenant includes making them free of fear and grief through abundant livelihood and victory over enemies, as the Torah states elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي في جعلكم ممن لا خوف عليهم و لا حزن بسعة العيش والنصر على الأعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must fear God alone and not stray into the fate of unbelievers; rahba is the soul's fear of expected harm from what it would flee.
rows.anchor: والرهب حذر النفس مما شأنها منه الهرب لأذى تتوقعه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the extended argument suits learned deniers and stubborn opponents, who resist what they know.
rows.anchor: وأطال سبحانه في حجاجهم جريا على قانون النظر في جدال العالم الجاحد وخطاب المنكر المعانج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing the revealed Qur'an, which confirms their scripture, reaffirms the truth of that Book.
rows.anchor: تقرير لذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says they must renew faith in the Qur'an because it supplies unseen details, especially of the afterlife, absent from their scripture; as the final Book, it completes explanations earlier scriptures left for later revelation.
rows.anchor: تجديد الإيمان بالقرآن لما فيه من إنباء بأمور من المغيبات التي لم تكن في كتابهم كتفاصيل أمور الآخرة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali links the opening severe command to the sudden harshness of the Hour, pairing the first warning blows of command with the first blows of creation.
rows.anchor: وهي أول قوارع الأمر كما أن فجاءة الساعة أول قوارع الخلق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The warned person either flees from the rebuke like wild donkeys from a lion or turns away arrogantly after reflection.
rows.anchor: إما أن ينفر عند الزجرة توحشا

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar says that minds are as if their Maker has undermined them; the author connects this to arrogant people being diverted from God's signs as punishment for pride.
rows.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه : لكنها عقول كادها باريها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The warning also teaches the attentive person to avoid public and hidden acts harmful in the afterlife, including exploitation, adultery, and intercourse during menstruation.
rows.anchor: تمام هذا المعنى ينهى المتأنس المحاصر عن الفواحش الظاهرة والباطنة الضارة في العقبى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The warning reaches conduct people regard as worldly cleverness, including consuming wealth unjustly, usury, spying, backbiting, and mockery.
rows.anchor: ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The prohibitions include falsely denying a believer's faith for worldly gain and preventing charitable giving by people of virtue and means.
rows.anchor: ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The discipline extends to refusing excess beyond sufficiency, including arrogance and coveting others' worldly display, because every surplus is a trial.
rows.anchor: لأن كل زائد على الكفاف فتنة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Mastery of this prohibition passage underlies later knowledge, action, steadfastness, and acceptance when tested.
rows.anchor: ولا تصح الوجوه والحروف التي بعده أي وهي سائر الحروف علما وعملا وثباتا وقبولا عند التمحيص إلا بحسب الإحكام في قراءة هذا الحرف

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The upright religion asks little in commands but requires strong abstention from limitless prohibitions, whose many avenues bring harm after death; people struggle because they mistake forbidden excess for worldly necessity.
rows.anchor: لأن الملة الحنيفية مبنية على الاكتفاء باليسير من المأمورات والمبالغة في الحمية من عموم ما لا يتناهى من المنهيات

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Abstinence is the foundation of treatment: worship without giving up prohibitions is like taking medicine without a diet, wasting the remedy and worsening the illness.
rows.anchor: والحمية أصل الدواء , فمن لم يحتم عن المنهيات لم ينفعه تداويه بالمأمورات

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: People may perform great acts of worship yet lose their effort because they pursued worldly desires and sins; worship without abstinence is treatment without a necessary diet.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يصومون ويصلون ويأخذون وهنا من الليل لكن ذلك تداو بغير حمية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: One who abstains has fulfilled the prohibition passage; the most beloved worship includes leaving worldly status and wealth's temptations, while the quoted sayings praise prophetic simplicity and adherence to the Sunnah.
rows.anchor: أحب العبادات إلى الله ترك الدنيا وحمية النفس من هوى جاهها ومالها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The Qur'an is evidence for the person who acts on it and leads him to Paradise, but becomes evidence against one who neglects it, driving him toward a terrifying pit of Hell.
rows.anchor: والقرآن حجة لمن عمل به فصار إمامه يقوده إلى الجنة . وحجة على من لم يعمل به

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a light by which God guides some and misguides others, and may increase wrongdoers' loss; the passage closes with a supplication seeking refuge in God's forgiveness and pleasure.
rows.anchor: ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به من نشاء من عبادنا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Keeping the commands and prohibitions that govern worldly welfare builds a virtuous habit that eases the afterlife's commands and prohibitions; belief in the unseen trades passing worldly goods for the promised lasting reward.
rows.anchor: فكل الحلال ما عدا الكفاف بالسنة متجر للعبد , إن أنفقه ربحه وأبقاه فقدم عليه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Worldly wealth is profitable when given away for the hereafter, as shown by the wish to give charity before death and the command to spend what one loves.
rows.anchor: لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The lawful sphere is broad so gratitude may be shown, while prohibitions restrict it to cultivate patience, making the servant both grateful and patient.
rows.anchor: حرف النهي مضيق لمتسع حرف الحلال ليحصل به الصبر

rows.speaker: حارثة
rows.claim: Haritha describes seeing Paradise's inhabitants enjoying bliss and Hell's inhabitants suffering as if before his eyes; this vision made worldly gold and pottery equal to him.
rows.anchor: كما قال حارثة : ( كأني أنظر إلى أهل الجنة في الجنة ينعمون وإلى أهل النار في النار يعذبون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inner vision of promised reward and punishment steadies the soul; true dreams and unveiling strengthen certainty that the eternal should be chosen over the transient.
rows.anchor: ليدع الفاني للباقي على يقين ومشاهدة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Umar grieved at the Prophet's condition, the Prophet asked whether he was content that others have this world while they have the hereafter.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعمر رضي الله عنه لما رثى لحاله : ( أما ترضى أن تكون لهم الدنيا ولنا الآخرة ؟ )

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Patience restrains the soul even from lawful desires; this is its purification, while exhausting it through restraint gives it life and indulging it corrupts it, as the sun chapter says.
rows.anchor: وصبر النفس عن شهواتها وإن كانت حلالا هو حقيقة تزكيتها , وقتلها بإضنائها منها هو حياتها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The soul is like a mount: restraint strengthens it and indulgence weakens it; lawful restraint applies broadly except to women and perfume.
rows.anchor: والنفس مطية يقويها إنضاؤها , ويضعفها استمتاعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes the prohibition on taking back even a large dowry from one's wife as a Qur'anic indication of the lawful marital exception.
rows.anchor: أتيتم إحداهن قنطارا فلا تأخذوا منه شيئا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Perfume is also excepted because it nourishes the spirit, strengthens the senses, and carries a breath from the unseen inward realm to the visible world.
rows.anchor: والثاني في الطيب , لأنه غذاء للروح وتقوية للحواس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Apart from those exceptions, indulging in lawful pleasures and following desire signifies denying the Merciful's promise and believing Satan's promises.
rows.anchor: وما عداهما فالاستمتاع به واتباع النفس هواها فيه علامة تكذيب وعد الرحمن وتصديق وعد الشيطان

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: In practical life, one should release possessions beyond sufficiency to the needy; extra capital may fund commerce or be reserved for need, without hoarding or constriction.
rows.anchor: رفعها عما زاد على الكفاف وتخليته لذوي الحاجة ليتخذوه معاشا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: More than two sets of clothing, for work and Friday, signals weak faith and departure from the Prophet's, caliphs', and righteous people's practice.
rows.anchor: اتخاذ أكثر من لبستين للمهنة والجمعة علامة لضعف الإيمان وخلاف السنة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: He criticizes culinary excess: selecting food for attractive appearance rather than sound knowledge and scrupulousness, multiplying condiments, and varying dishes.
rows.anchor: وكذلك تصفية لباب الطعام وقصد المستحسن في الصورة دون المستحسن في العلم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Restraint also means one residence and sufficient farmland, avoiding tall buildings and ostentatious displays.
rows.anchor: وكذلك اتخاذ أكثر من مسكن واحد وأكثر من مزدرع كاف ورفع البناء والاستشراف بالمباني

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet once refused to return a man's greeting because he had built a dome in Medina, until the man demolished it and leveled it with other homes.
rows.anchor: امتنع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من رد السلام على رجل اتخذ قبة في المدينة حتى هدمها وسواها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The world is a prison for the believer: recognizing its confinement prompts seeking release to the afterlife; failing to recognize it encourages a futile desire to remain.
rows.anchor: وإنما الدنيا للمؤمن سجن إن شعر به وضيق فيه على نفسه طلبت السراح منه إلى الآخرة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Horses bring reward to a fighter, sin to an ostentatious owner, and no blame to one who keeps them for necessary affairs.
rows.anchor: والخيل ثلاثة : أجر للمجاهد , ووزر على المباهي , وعفو للمستكفي بها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Keeping surplus grazing livestock breaks with Prophetic practice, burdens the needy, and accumulates goods meant only to sustain a sufficient livelihood.
rows.anchor: والزيادة على الكفاف من النعم السائمة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says his household kept one hundred sheep and did not seek increase, sacrificing one sheep when a lamb was born.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لنا غنم مائة لا نريد أن تزيد , فإذا ولد الراعي بهمة ذبحنا مكانها شاة )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says whoever hoards food for forty days has disavowed God and God disavows him.
rows.anchor: ( من احتكر طعاما أربعين يوما فقد برئ من الله وبرئ الله منه )

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Ordinary goods may be stored and money invested, but food and necessities may be brought in without being hoarded to make money; doing so is hoarding.
rows.anchor: فالأمتعة تجلب وتختزن ويستنمى فيه الدينار والدراهم , والطعام والقوام يجلب ولا يختزن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: What one must not gaze at longingly is even more strongly forbidden to grasp; restraint of the heart, inner vision, soul, and hand completes reading the prohibition passage.
rows.anchor: فبهذه الأمور من إيمان القلب ورؤية الفؤاد وصبر النفس وكف اليد عن الانبساط في التمول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukūʿ may stand for prayer as a whole because it is distinctive of this community; the command can therefore mean praying in congregation, with added emphasis on joining the group.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالركوع الصلاة , عبر عنها به لما ذكر من خصوص هذه الأمة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling Israel's favors and prohibiting ingratitude and broken covenants, God rebukes their scholars for urging virtues and prohibiting vices while failing to practice what they preach.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يأمرون غيرهم بما يزعمون أنه تزكية وينهونه عما يدعون أنه تردية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines commanding as imposing a judgment and righteousness as expansion in good deeds; forgetting is a lapse after knowledge has been gained.
rows.anchor: من الأمر وهو الإلزام بالحكم - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likely target is Torah's command to follow Muhammad: scholars imposed Torah's other rulings on ordinary people while neglecting the foundational righteousness on which the rest depends.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد به حكم التوراة , كانوا يحملون عوامهم عليه وهم يعلمون دون العوام أن من حكم التوراة اتباع محمد

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Some advised seekers to follow Muhammad but did not follow their own advice; this exposes irrationality and links their conduct to their earlier breach of covenant, confusion, and concealment.
rows.anchor: فيهم من أشار على من استهداه بالهداية لاتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يهدوا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The clause about reciting scripture shows that the Torah's instruction to follow Muhammad is explicit, not hidden by implication, and makes a scholar's disobedience more heinous.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : فيه إشعار بأن أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في منطوق تلاوته ليس في خفي إفهامه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Tilāwa means following a speaker's utterance from its beginning; the circumstantial clause emphasizes their knowledge of scripture while they disobey.
rows.anchor: من التلاوة , وهو تتبع قول قائل أول من جهة أوليته

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Reason grasps the realities whose outward surface the senses perceive; it is called reason because it restrains a person from stumbling into ruin.
rows.anchor: والعقل إدراك حقائق ما نال الحس ظاهره

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Their attachment to leadership made them resist becoming followers of Arabs after seeing themselves as masters of the earth, so patience is prescribed to compel them to accept following truth.
rows.anchor: ما تعودت به أنفسهم من الرياسة والتقدم فلما في ذلك عليهم من المشقة أن يصيروا أتباعا للعرب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Patience helps them demonstrate truth and submit to it by restraining the soul from habit and desire and purifying it; this light lets the heart see beyond the panic of leaving familiar ways and includes fasting and other patience.
rows.anchor: والصبر حبس النفس عن حاجتها وعادتها وعلى إصلاحها وتزكيتها , هو ضياء للقلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer connects the worshipper to the highest station.
rows.anchor: أي الموصلة إلى المقام الأعلى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: True prayer restrains its practitioner from falsehood and commands holding to truth and returning to it; prayer with this quality, supported by patience against desire, leads to salvation.
rows.anchor: من لم تنهه صلاته عن ركوب الباطل والتمادي فيه وتأمره بلزوم الحق والرجوع إليه فليس بمصل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Prayer is mentioned second because it is provision from God, sparing them from buying silence or concealment from their followers; the command to persist in family prayer promises that God provides.
rows.anchor: وثنى بالصلاة لأنها استرزاق يغنيهم عن اشتراء ثمن كانوا يأخذونه من أتباعهم في اللبس والكتمان
